findings.F1: The tested effect is not in the data: on up hours, the 4-hour excess return barely changes across the hour's (rise in usual moves × volume ratio) quantiles, from -1.9 bp (t -1.23, n 7694) in the bottom half to +10.6 bp (t 0.44, n 154) in the top 1 %, and up hours with z>3 and volume ratio>3 give -3.5 bp at 4 hours (t -0.18, n 203), so the move per case (total +0.01 %) is 0.1 times the 0.11 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: The book's loss comes from its fees: it is in position on 49 % of bars at a mean allocation of 0.70 and turns over 2.85 times its value per coin-day; its gross gain is about 5.6 bp a day against about 15.7 bp a day of fees; only 19 % of its in-position bars carry a forecast of 10 or more.
findings.F3: The book also gives up the market's own rise: its mean daily return is -3.3 bp in 2020 against +52.4 bp for holding, -3.7 bp in 2023 against +25.7 bp, and +0.7 bp in 2021 against +38.2 bp, so its Sharpe ends 1.42 below holding's.
findings.F4: The opposite side carries a graded effect: after down hours, the 4-hour excess return rises with the hour's (fall in usual moves × volume ratio), from -0.7 bp (n 7605) in the bottom half to +16.9 bp (t 1.38, n 456) in the 95–98 % band and +66.2 bp (t 1.91, n 153) in the top 1 %; that last figure is about 0.4 of the 4-hour usual move (1.42 % for BTC, 1.82 % for ETH) and 6 times the cost of a trade.
findings.F5: The same rebound shows over 2 hours, at +15.5 bp (t 2.24, n 911) in the 95–98 % band and +26.6 bp (t 1.87, n 304) in the top 1 %; down hours with z<-3 and volume ratio>3 give +20.1 bp at 2 hours (t 1.81, n 432) and +47.0 bp at 4 hours (t 1.88, n 230).
findings.F6: The rebound after the top 5 % of heavy-volume down hours holds on both coins, BTC at +22.5 bp (t 1.62, n 373) and ETH at +26.8 bp (t 1.58, n 388), and is positive in 5 of 8 years (2021 +149.6 bp, t 2.75; 2023 +25.8 bp, t 2.20), but it is negative in 2025 (-22.7 bp, t -1.32), and its rank correlation with the surge's size among down hours with a volume ratio above 2 is only 0.057.

ideas.idea: After an hour in which the coin falls far more than its typical hourly move over the past 30 days, on volume several times its average hourly volume over the past 30 days, the price rebounds over the next four hours. The larger that hour's fall relative to its typical 30-day hourly move times its volume relative to its 30-day average, the larger the rebound.
ideas.consequence: A heavy-volume hourly plunge is a reason to buy for about four hours rather than sell into it, since in its most extreme cases the rebound is several times the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: heavy-volume plunge rebounds

ideas.idea: After an hour in which the coin falls far more than its typical hourly move over the past 30 days, on volume several times its average hourly volume over the past 30 days, the price rebounds over the next two hours, more the more extreme the fall and the volume are together.
ideas.consequence: A heavy-volume hourly plunge supports a short long position of about two hours, which catches most of the rebound with less time exposed.
ideas.name: plunge rebound two hours
